messages:
jing: heads-up: onboarding issue with Narwhal13b mixed-quant build. downstream summarization tests showing entity swap hallucinations :eyes:
mae: uhoh. can you paste a minimal repro or a diff from the fp16 run?
jing: repro is tiny — run summary benchmark on our sample doc set (news-100). int4 backbone + int3 per-head on attention. FP16 baseline is clean. Hybrid quant shows entity A->B swaps ~12% of samples.
ryan: what quant tool did you use? quant-sieve or oqt?
jing: quant-sieve v0.9.2 with headwise-int3 flag. conversion script: `python tools/quantize.py --model narwhal13b --scheme hybrid --headwise int3 --rest int4`
eva: any differences in rotary params or head dim layout? those swaps smell like misaligned KV positions.
jing: found this in the conversion log: `rotary_scale: serialized as float16 per-head (len=64)` but runtime expects single global float32 scale for head groups.
mae: oh that mismatch can subtly change attention phase for some heads. Did we validate per-head ordering after export?
jing: not until now. I dumped head order map and token alignments. Some heads got shuffled by the exporter because of permutation compression in quant-sieve.
ryan: hmm. permutation + per-head rotary scale quantization => different phase offsets per head. That could flip sign on specific frequency components -> entity slot swaps.
jing: exactly. quick diff from fp16 run: `attn_head_17_phase_cos ~ -0.002 fp16 vs 0.998 hybrid` (bad).
mae: can we force rotary_scale to be broadcasted (single value) on load as a temporary mitigation?
jing: tried that: forcing broadcasted scale reduced swap rate to ~2% but increased perplexity a bit. tradeoff might be acceptable for now.
eva: we should also ensure conversion preserves head ordering. propose adding an assert in quant-sieve: `assert head_order_map == canonical_head_order` failing conversion if mismatch found.
triage-bot: regression-alert: summarization-suite: entity-swap-rate increased by 9.8% on narwhal13b-hybrid at 2024-11-09T14:05:21Z
ryan: good call, add canonical ordering check + a normalization step that coerces rotary_scale dtype to float32 and broadcast if exporter created per-head array.
mae: long-term: we should support per-head rotary scales in runtime but with careful calibration step (recompute phase calibration after quantization). For now, change quant-sieve to output `rotary_scale: {type: broadcast, value: X}` by default for hybrid schemes.
jing: I opened a PR with the assert + broadcast fallback: https://github.com/redwood/quant-sieve/pull/142 (WIP) — unit tests added for headmap identity.
eva: add a reproducer snippet so QA can run locally:

# reproducer
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
resp = c.generate(model='narwhal13b-hybrid', prompt=open('news-100/01.txt').read(), max_tokens=80)
print(resp.text)

mae: also try forcing first-attn-layer to fp16 in hybrid profile to see if that stabilizes entity slots (we've seen that help before).
jing: noted. running a small sweep now (first-5k tokens). will post results. thanks y'all :pray:
devops-bot: deployment note: rolling back narwhal13b-hybrid to serveless-fp16 is scheduled in 10m if no fix lands.
ryan: if the broadcast mitigation looks good, we can patch conversion and re-quantize nightly to avoid rollback.
jing: update: broadcast mitigates most cases, still seeing 1-2% swaps on long multi-entity stories. I'm going to log headwise phase deltas to trace which heads remain unstable and drop int3 on those specific heads as a surgical mitigation.
eva: sounds reasonable. please tag me on the PR and add the head list in the commit message.
jing: will do. follow-up once sweep completes (ETA ~30m).
